headline: Congress cancels a 2024 federal decision that had limited oil and gas leasing in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge's Coastal Plain.
what_it_does: This law uses the Congressional Review Act to cancel a December 2024 Bureau of Land Management decision on oil and gas leasing in the Coastal Plain of Alaska's Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. That 2024 decision had closed about 1.2 million of the area's roughly 1.6 million acres to leasing and exploration, leaving the legal minimum of 400,000 acres open. The 2024 decision had replaced a 2020 decision that made all 1.6 million acres available. Canceling the 2024 decision opens more of the area to oil and gas leasing.

who_it_affects.how: More acres in the refuge's Coastal Plain may be available for them to lease, explore, and develop.
The agency can no longer use the 2024 decision to run the Coastal Plain leasing program and its limits on where leasing is allowed.

who_it_affects.group: People who live near or use the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge
who_it_affects.how: Land the 2024 decision had set aside to protect resources and certain uses may now be open to oil and gas activity.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 11, 2025; the 2024 decision is treated as having no force or effect.
